newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - February 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - February 13.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Hindustan Times
TEN-MEMBER PUNJAB MINISTRY SWORN IN

Prakash Singh Badal was sworn in as chief minister of Punjab, along with nine cabinet ministers. This was the third time that Badal took over the reins of the state, the earlier occasions being in 1970 and 1977. While his first term lasted only 15 months, the second term saw him in office for 32 months.
Indian Express
CONGRESS ON ROAD TO DECLINE

The recently concluded by-elections and the Punjab assembly elections may well mark a watershed in the nation's political life. They mark the end of Congress party chief Sitaram Kesri's prime ministerial ambitions and could herald the beginning of the end of the Bharatiya Janata Party's (BJP) untouchable status. Furthermore, they have given breathing space to Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda, whose continuation has come under a cloud ever since Kesri took over the reins of the Congress. The immediate fallout from the Punjab victory was likely to be felt by the BJP in the forthcoming municipal polls in Delhi.
The Economic Times
FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS ADVISED TO DIVEST OF DEFAULTERS

Financial institutions (FIs) should consider divestment of stakes in firms where there are recurring or large defaults on loans, an expert panel report suggested. Divestment should also be considered in the case of non-payment of dividend and where there was a continuous and large decline in share prices in relation to the market index, it said.
COMPROMISE LIKELY ON TATA-SINGAPORE AIRLINES VENTURE

A compromise, proposed by the Civil Aviation Ministry, to allow Tata-Singapore Airlines (SIA) to operate in the domestic civil aviation sector as a special case has been sent to the Finance Ministry for approval. The proposal is likely to find place in the modified cabinet note, which is being drafted. The note, favouring the Tata-SIA proposal, identified areas of concern for the state-owned domestic carrier Indian Airlines.
Financial Express
VIABILITY OF REORGANISING MUTUAL FUNDS TO BE STUDIED

The bourse regulator has decided to set up a committee to address the possibility of giving mutual funds the alternative of reorganising as companies. This followed discussions with trustees of all the registered mutual funds where some of them felt the current three-tier system of organising mutual funds (promoter, trustees and asset management companies) could be scrapped for better efficiency.
UNIT TRUST TO SET UP THREE ASSET MANAGEMENT FIRMS

The Unit Trust of India (UTI) will float three asset management companies (AMCs) to manage its mutual fund schemes, including the 150 billion rupee US64. UTI, India's largest mutual fund organisation, has submitted its plans to the bourse regulator for approval. Each of the AMCs would be given a balanced portfolio of different growth and income schemes to manage. UTI has also decided to set up a separate company for entering the insurance sector when it is opened up. The venture would be in collaboration with a foreign partner.
BRAND EQUITY FUND MAY END UP REDUCING DEFICIT
The funds allocated and raised for promotion of Indian products overseas are expected to contribute to bridging the gap in the budgetary deficit for fiscal 1996/97 (April-March).
Business Standard
LIFE INSURANCE CORP MAY RECAST PORTFOLIO

The Life Insurance Corporation (LIC) plans to change the composition of its investment portfolio. The proposal is significant as the state-owned firm's total investments at the end of 1995/96 (April-March) were estimated at 727.8 billion rupees. The proposed changes mean a decline in the share of state and union government securities in LIC's total investment portfolio from the present 50 percent and a corresponding increase in investments in approved securities.
TATAS TO INVEST 35 BLN RUPEES IN AUTO VENTURES

The Tatas will invest 30-35 billion rupees to promote a slew of companies to supply components to their car manufacturing venture. The vehicle was scheduled to be launched next year. The firms would be promoted by Tata Autocomp Systems (TACO), the holding company. The venture would have a two-tier structure with the first tier consisting of mostly 50:50 joint ventures with global auto ancillary leaders. These firms would focus on technology absorption, design, engineering and indigenous research and development. The second tier would consist of manufacturing ventures with mainly Indian partners.
CALL RATES JUMP, EXPECTING HEAVY BOND REDEMPTION

The redemption of India Development Bonds (IDB) due on Saturday had an impact on the call money market which touched a high of 8.5 percent. Almost 50 percent of the remaining IDBs worth $1.8 billion was likely to be redeemed in rupees on February 15. On January 15, $418 million worth IDBs was due for redemption of which, $231 million was redeemed in rupees.
DESTEC ENERGY TO INVEST $2 BLN IN INDIAN POWER SECTOR

Texas-based Destec Energy planned to enter the Indian power sector by investing about $2 billion in power-generating projects. Destec, an associate of the Fortune 500 firm Dow Chemicals, became the latest power giant to plan major investments in recent times. Destec's Indian representative said it planned to put up plants only in west and south India. The company would focus on setting up power plants of above 500 mw capacity as well as small captive plants for industries which require assured power supply, he added.
The Observer
TEAM GOING TO PAKISTAN FOR TALKS

The prospects for an overland gas pipeline project between Iran and India have brightened as Pakistan showed its willingness to allow the pipeline to pass over its territory. Official sources said the governments of India, Iran and Pakistan have agreed in principle to pursue the matter in right earnest. It was understood that Pakistan had indicated to the governments of India and Iran that it would not raise any objection over the passage of the proposed pipeline.
